items.text: The [[p:Superior Electoral Court]] declared [[p:Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva|Lula]] re-elected in the [[e:2026 Brazilian general election|runoff]] with 51.79% to 48.21% for [[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]]. Bolsonaro says he does not recognise the result and will seek annulment, citing a Supreme Court order that extended voting by two hours in some sections.
items.notes: Annulment pledge reported by O Liberal: https://www.oliberal.com/eleicoes/flavio-bolsonaro-nao-reconhece-derrota-e-promete-pedir-anulacao-da-eleicao-1.1186879 . O Liberal notes his own campaign had sought extensions in five states. Trump declined to say whom he backed.

items.text: In the [[e:2026 Serbian parliamentary election|snap election]], preliminary results with 96.2% counted give the Student List 52.54% and [[p:Aleksandar Vučić]]'s list 39.29%, on 68.8% turnout. Vučić conceded on election night; Euronews projects about 140 of 250 seats for the Student List.
items.notes: Seat projection is Euronews's (Ljubiša Ivanović). Vučić's current office is described inconsistently (resigned presidency in September per earlier log).

items.text: With 95% of protocols processed in the [[e:2026 Bulgarian presidential election|presidential election]], [[p:Iliana Iotova]] has 34.6% and PP-DB-backed Andrey Gyurov 32.0%, ahead of [[p:Kostadin Kostadinov]] on 12.6%. Turnout was about 20–22%; the runoff is on 1 Nov.
items.notes: Partial CEC count; certification of runoff tickets within 48 hours.

items.text: Saudi defence minister [[p:Khalid bin Salman]], Pakistan's army chief [[p:Asim Munir]] and Turkish intelligence chief [[p:İbrahim Kalın]] held security talks in Tehran, with Qatari mediators coordinating with Washington. The aim is to avert renewed US/Israeli–Iranian fighting; no outcome was reported. Trump said on 25 Oct there would be 'no strike today'.
items.notes: Gulf News puts Brent at about $114.6 on 26 Oct, down from >$117.

items.text: CNN, citing US and Israeli sources, reports that [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] lobbied Trump for a joint strike on Iran before the 27 Oct election and that Trump asked him to wait. Channel 12 reported that army chief [[p:Eyal Zamir]] resisted the plan; Netanyahu's office called this fake news and [[p:Israel Katz]] denied any pre-election attack plan.
items.outlet: Times of Israel (relaying CNN and Channel 12)
items.notes: Anonymous-source reports, denied by Netanyahu's office and Katz. CNN not opened directly.

items.text: Opposition leader [[p:María Corina Machado]] returned to Venezuela after more than 10 months abroad and appeared with supporters in Lara state. [[p:Marco Rubio]] credited US-backed talks with [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]]'s interim government; no election date is set.
[[p:Marine Le Pen]] launched her campaign for the [[e:2027 French presidential election]] in Orléans, proposing a national-unity government with [[p:Jordan Bardella]] as prime minister.
items.notes: Sources don't explain how her ineligibility ruling was resolved; election dates given differ (April vs May 2027). Check.

items.text: Kremlin aide [[p:Yuri Ushakov]] told state TV that Moscow will be ready to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US after 4 Nov, Russia's [[e:Unity Day (Russia)|Unity Day]]. He called the first meeting a 'trial run' and said a settlement must also involve Europe.
items.notes: Interview with Pavel Zarubin (VGTRK). Meduza notes the timing falls after the 3 Nov US midterms. Russian quote on Europe translated.

items.text: In a TSN interview, [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] set out his positions for the talks: no limits on the army and no neutrality, and if NATO membership is blocked, US and European Article 5-style guarantees. He proposed an energy ceasefire, a new Black Sea grain deal and more prisoner exchanges, and warned that easing sanctions first would weaken Kyiv.
items.notes: Interview by Alla Mazur (1+1). Also said Patriot deliveries are 'very slow' and he wants an army of up to 800,000. Cross-check is a personal desk note (weak).

items.text: US envoy [[p:Steve Witkoff]] met [[p:Vladimir Putin]] for about three hours in St Petersburg, a day after meeting Zelensky and Europeans in Oslo. Ushakov says Witkoff relayed 'new aspects' of the European and Ukrainian positions.
Ushakov says preparations have begun for a Putin–Trump–Xi meeting, possibly at APEC in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov. Trump has said he would go mainly to discuss nuclear arms control.
items.notes: Kremlin claim; WSJ says Putin proposed it on 9 Oct. LIGA.net said 'December', a discrepancy.

items.text: The Telegraph, citing diplomats, reports that Moscow wants to use the talks to press NATO to roll back its posture to 1997 levels, including from Poland, the Baltics and Finland. European officials told the paper NATO will not agree.
items.notes: Anonymous sources. Also reports Witkoff offered to discuss easing sanctions on Russian fuel exports.

items.text: Ahead of the Oleshky ceasefire, ombudsman [[p:Dmytro Lubinets]] leads Ukraine's team and Yana Lantratova Russia's. The deal covers a ceasefire including the access route, aid deliveries, and demining with free exit, in stages. [[p:Valery Gerasimov]] ordered a halt to fire on the Kherson axis from 04:00 Moscow time on 27 Oct.
items.notes: White House estimates 1,700–2,000 residents remain. Zelensky expects Moscow to steer evacuees toward Russia.

items.text: [[p:Elon Musk]] claimed Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms by using it for offensive drone strikes and said the 'loophole' was closed. Ukrainian officials deny it. ISW says Ukraine's interception rate against jet drones fell from about 77% to 74% during the 14–24 Oct disruption.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Zelensky confirmed Starshield at full speed. Ukraine's armed forces told Meduza the claim is 'technically impossible'.

items.text: [[p:Institute for the Study of War|ISW]], relying mainly on observer Kostiantyn Mashovets, reports Ukrainian forces retook Perebudova, Komar and Fedorivka on the Oleksandrivka axis, and that Russia pulled units from its Huliaipole and Druzhkivka pushes in response. It also reports Russian infiltration widening in central Dobropillia and gains near Filiia.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Analysis. A Russian milblogger claims Bilytske taken; not confirmed by ISW.

items.text: Ukraine's General Staff reported 193 combat clashes on 24 Oct, most on the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka and Huliaipole axes, and puts Russian losses at 1,990 for the day.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Ukrainian military claim.

items.text: Russia's defence ministry claims its Vostok group took Obshchee in Zaporizhzhia region, after claiming Myrivka on 22 Oct, and claims strikes on a Kharkiv substation and a bridge near Zaporizhzhia.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Russian military claim; Reuters could not verify the ship strike claims.

items.text: Ukrainian strikes hit industry deep in Russia. Perm's governor reports 'minor damage' and five hurt at a plant monitoring channels name as titanium maker [[p:VSMPO-Avisma]] in Berezniki, over 1,400 km from the border. A missile strike, reportedly [[p:Storm Shadow]], hit Yelets's Energiya plant, and Belgorod's governor reports 3 dead in the city.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Belgorod toll differs: Meduza says 2 dead. Target identifications from monitoring channels. Meduza counts 500+ drones over Russia overnight.

items.text: Voronezh's governor says a drone attack killed two and injured 17, most on a train hit by debris, with 113 drones recorded. OSINT channels name aircraft and synthetic rubber plants as targets; unverified.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes

items.text: Ukraine's air force says Russia launched 140 drones (about half jet-powered) and four missiles overnight, with 112 drones downed and 15 sites hit. [[p:Ukrenergo]] imposed hourly outages in parts of the country, citing 'massive Russian attacks'. Strikes on 25 Oct killed 8 and injured 51, per the Kyiv Independent.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Air Force figures. Odesa firefighters hit in a double-tap strike.

items.text: Zelensky submitted bills to the [[p:Verkhovna Rada]] extending [[e:Martial law in Ukraine|martial law]] and general mobilisation by 90 days, from 31 Oct to 29 Jan 2027. The Rada must vote before 31 Oct.
items.notes: Bills 16182 and 16183.

items.text: [[p:National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine|NABU]] and SAP searched the National Bank, including Governor [[p:Andriy Pyshnyi]]'s office. The bank says no one was detained or charged; MP Yaroslav Zhelezniak has called for Pyshnyi's resignation.
items.notes: Anonymous sources link it to the Karpatnaftokhim and Sense Bank cases. A reported resignation letter was denied by the NBU. Possible Rada discussion on 26 Oct not confirmed.

items.text: In 'Operation Carthage', NABU and SAP charged a former department head at the Prosecutor General's Office with collecting over UAH 1bn in bribes from fraudulent call centres the office allegedly protected.
items.notes: Former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko resigned over the case in September.

items.text: The [[p:Central Bank of Russia|Bank of Russia]] held its key rate at 14%, citing high inflation expectations and budget uncertainty. It forecasts 2026 GDP growth of 0.5–1% and inflation of 7.1–7.6%.
[[p:United Russia]] will back the 2027–29 federal budget at its first Duma reading on 29 Oct. The draft has a 2027 deficit of about 5.5 trillion rubles.

Deputy PM [[p:Alexander Novak]] said Russia could supply as much diesel as the US wants, and that three tankers are already heading to the US East Coast. Lithuania's [[p:Gitanas Nausėda]] called the deal 'a bad day'.
items.notes: Kpler expects the first cargo in New York around 7 Nov.

items.text: Ambrey and the IMO told the FT that over 570 vessels have been struck in the Black Sea in 2026, killing at least 40 sailors, and that Russia accounts for about 90% of strikes on civilian shipping since 10 Sept.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: FT original (paywalled) not read.

items.text: The [[p:North Atlantic Council]] agreed to send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar and drones to the Black Sea after drone strikes on merchant ships off Bulgaria and Romania, plus intelligence and explosives-forensics teams. NATO has not formally attributed the attacks; Russia denies involvement.
items.notes: Bulgaria says US P-8 patrols have begun. Rubio and Rutte discussed Black Sea security on 22 Oct (State Dept readout). Romanian search for three missing KHORYV crew suspended 24 Oct (G4Media).

items.text: A Ukrainian drone with explosives, apparently diverted by Russian jamming during an attack on St Petersburg, entered Lithuania from Polish airspace on 18 Oct and crashed, damaging a car. PM [[p:Mindaugas Sinkevičius]] has asked NATO for consultations on shooting down radar-tracked objects without visual identification.
items.notes: Ukraine apologised. Sinkevičius expects a rule change 'probably within a month'.

items.text: An arson attempt failed at a Lithuanian firm storing Starlink equipment; Sinkevičius blamed Russia. It follows arson at a Starlink ground station in Poland in September, where Poland has now detained a Ukrainian suspect, and at Starlink antennas near Sofia.
items.notes: Russian attribution is claimed by Lithuanian and Polish officials. A Bulgarian court issued arrest warrants for two Germans; sources differ on the Bulgarian date (9 or 13 Oct).

items.text: German prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian man suspected of spying for Russian intelligence on arms production and eastern-flank facilities. Der Spiegel says he was interested in the German brigade deploying to Lithuania.

A resident found a foreign drone's wreckage in a forest near the Russian border in Alūksne municipality, days after the army called off a search. Police opened a criminal case and the army an internal inquiry.
items.notes: Defence minister Raivis Melnis suggested it was shot down over Russia and glided in (translation).

items.text: Latvia declared a brief airspace alert over Krāslava and Rēzekne districts. The cabinet agreed to extend conscription to the State Border Guard from 2028.
After two critical PHP vulnerabilities were disclosed, Finland, Latvia and Lithuania took many state websites offline as a precaution. Officials say no exploitation was confirmed.

Russian military satellite Cosmos 2612 manoeuvred close to an [[p:ICEYE]] radar satellite believed to supply imagery to Ukraine; LeoLabs put the closest approach at about 500 m and called it potentially dangerous. An Estonian MP called it a deliberate provocation.
items.notes: Distance disputed: some reports claim tens of metres.

items.text: A drone carrying explosives crashed near a house in Telenești district. Moldova's foreign ministry called it a serious violation of sovereignty and will expel a Russian embassy employee.
items.notes: No Russian reaction reported.

items.text: [[p:Maia Sandu]] made her first official visit to Hungary for the 1956 anniversary at [[p:Péter Magyar]]'s invitation. No agreements were reported.

73 former political prisoners, including [[p:Maria Kalesnikava]] and [[p:Viktar Babaryka]], urged EU, UK, Swiss and Norwegian leaders to work actively for the release of the roughly 900 still held, using negotiation and incentives alongside pressure.
items.notes: Signatory Marina Zolatava called 'sanctions or negotiations' a false dilemma (translation).

items.text: Polish prosecutors charged a second Georgian man with aiding the June murder of Russian dissident cartoonist Robert Kuzovkov in Biała Podlaska. Both suspects deny the charges.
items.notes: No ordering party identified.

items.text: Two foreign men suspected of photographing anti-drone firm MyDefence in Aalborg for a suspected Russian intelligence contact were released, but charges stand.

Germany is practising rapid reinforcement of Estonia by land, sea and air for the first time (Brave Blue 26). Defence minister [[p:Martin Herem]] says HIMARS rockets have arrived but ATACMS deliveries remain on hold.
items.notes: Herem also said Estonia may need about a dozen light fighters against jet drones.

items.text: Norway adopted the EU's 21st sanctions package, adding 33 Russian and 22 third-country financial institutions and powers to list ships servicing shadow-fleet tankers.

Sinkevičius says Russia is testing how far it can go without triggering NATO collective defence; he agreed a direct line with Poland's PM. LRT reports Vilnius wants 1,500–2,000 permanently based US troops.
items.notes: link2 is analysis.
